eyebrow: ATOBAR · Agentic Teams On BYOK And Repos
title: How ATOBAR runs your GitHub issues
question: What happens, step by step, across a GitHub issue run and inside the Nano harness?
intro: ATOBAR stands for Agentic Teams On BYOK And Repos. Collaborators bring their own encrypted language model keys, plan work in GitHub issues, and let isolated cloud machines write, visually test, and merge code.
Step through each journey below using Next, Play, or the slider. Every step updates the screen preview and highlights changed database values in yellow.
subject: atobar-flow · 5-package Python monorepo (contracts, flow-engine, control-panel, flow-agent, atobar-ops)

roles.name: Collaborator
roles.about: writes GitHub issues and brings model keys

roles.name: GitHub Repo
roles.about: holds code, issues, pull requests, and two workflow files

roles.name: Control Panel
roles.about: public gateway and KMS key vault

roles.name: Flow Engine
roles.about: deterministic Python state machine and merge gate

roles.name: Spot Sandbox
roles.about: isolated cloud virtual machine running one agent role

terms.onboard.sh: The five-minute setup script that connects a GitHub repository to atobar-flow.
terms.flow-trigger.yml: The GitHub Actions workflow file in your repo that forwards issue labels and comments to atobar-flow.
terms.flow-metrics.yml: The GitHub Actions workflow file in your repo that runs metric checks and sends numeric results to atobar-flow.
terms.ATOBAR_TENANT_TOKEN: The secret token saved in your GitHub repo so its workflows can talk to the Control Panel.
terms.tenant_llm_keys: The Control Panel database table that stores encrypted API keys.
terms.tenant_role_llm: The Control Panel database table that maps each agent role to a model provider and model name.
terms.SotaWiki: The per-repo Knowledge Engine snapshot (purpose, stack, layout, invariants, and Mermaid diagram) injected so any BYOK model follows your repo's best practices.
terms.assess_issue_sufficiency: The deterministic Python function in flow-engine that checks if an issue is detailed enough to skip planning.
terms.flow-plan: The structured markdown checklist comment that the Planner role posts on a GitHub issue.
terms.flow:needs-approval: The GitHub label that pauses an issue until a human approves the plan.
terms.flow:approved: The GitHub label a human adds to approve a plan and start the Developer role.
terms.prepare_role_worktree: The sandbox function that creates a clean git folder for the next role on a warm machine.
terms.WARM_HANDOVER_FORBIDDEN_ROLES: The rule in contracts that blocks Evaluator and Arbitrator from reusing a Developer machine.
terms.flow-ack: The comment the Developer role posts on a pull request to report which review findings it fixed.
terms.flow-verdict: The comment the Evaluator role posts on a pull request after running static and visual checks.
terms.xwininfo: The Linux X11 tool that lists real open windows on the display server.
terms.arbitrate: The pure Python function in contracts that checks if all business metrics pass before merging.
terms.loop_rounds: The Flow Engine database table that records tokens, cost, and state for every agent turn.
terms.tenant_goals: The Flow Engine database table that tracks repository metric goals and spend caps.
terms.goal_step: The pure Python function in flow-engine that checks if all repository target metrics are met after a merge.
terms.NanobotRuntime: The headless runner in flow-agent that executes each agent role through the nanobot-ai Python SDK.
terms.nanobot_home: The isolated folder outside your client repository where the Nano harness keeps SOUL.md and session memory.
terms.SOUL.md: The per-run persona and rule file written into nanobot_home for the active agent role.
terms.tools_mcp: The out-of-process stdio FastMCP server that enforces per-role tool allowlists.
terms.view_image: The workspace-jailed multimodal image reader that lets the Evaluator inspect real X11 screenshots.
terms.FlowHook: The lifecycle hook around every Nano turn that tracks heartbeats, stalls, and per-tool token spend.

sections.title: J1: Onboarding a repo and encrypting BYOK keys
intro: A repository admin connects a GitHub repo in five minutes and stores encrypted language model keys in the Control Panel vault.
Today keys route per repo and per role. Per-invoking-user key billing and profile default keys are on the Vision roadmap.
sections.screenLabel: What you see in GitHub & Control Panel

steps.label: install GitHub App
steps.say: You install the atobar-flow-agent GitHub App on your repository and run onboard.sh inside a local clone.
steps.screen:
GitHub App: atobar-flow-agent installed on owner/repo
$ curl -fsSL .../onboard.sh | bash

steps.label: register repo & mint token
steps.say: You add the repository in the Control Panel. The Control Panel creates a tenant token and stores only its hash.
steps.screen:
Control Panel: owner/repo registered
Token minted: atb_9f8a... (shown once)

steps.label: save ATOBAR_TENANT_TOKEN
steps.say: The setup script saves ATOBAR_TENANT_TOKEN in your repository's GitHub Actions secrets.
steps.screen: GitHub Secret saved: ATOBAR_TENANT_TOKEN

steps.label: save API key & role models
steps.say: You paste your provider key. The Control Panel encrypts it with AWS KMS and saves it in tenant_llm_keys, then maps roles in tenant_role_llm.
steps.screen:
KMS Vault: claude & gemini keys sealed (AES-GCM)
Role routing: developer → claude, evaluator → gemini

steps.label: start onboarder role
steps.say: Flow Engine starts the onboarder role on a Spot machine. The onboarder scans your repo layout and conventions to build the SotaWiki Knowledge Engine map.
steps.screen: Spot Onboarder: Knowledge Engine (Mermaid SotaWiki) compiled

steps.label: open trigger & metrics PRs
steps.say: Setup opens pull requests for flow-trigger.yml and flow-metrics.yml once Flow Engine compiles your metric. Merging them activates the repo.
steps.screen: Workflows Active: .github/workflows/flow-trigger.yml + flow-metrics.yml

sections.title: J2: Jumbo Issue planning and the Spec-Sufficiency Gate
intro: Collaborators plan work directly in GitHub Issues. A deterministic Python check decides whether the issue needs a Planner run first or can go straight to coding.
sections.screenLabel: What you see on the GitHub Issue

steps.label: add label flow:feature
steps.say: You open an issue on GitHub and apply the label flow:needs-approval or a start label, or mention the bot in a comment.
steps.screen: Issue #42: Add rate-limit circuit breaker · flow:feature

steps.label: POST /v1/events
steps.say: The workflow flow-trigger.yml forwards the signed event to the Control Panel, which verifies the token and sends it to Flow Engine.
steps.screen: Webhook ingress: POST /v1/events verified

steps.label: assess_issue_sufficiency()
steps.say: Flow Engine runs assess_issue_sufficiency in pure Python. Concrete specs with file targets go straight to Developer; broad specs route to Planner.
steps.screen: Spec-Sufficiency Gate (0 LLM): Broad spec detected → route to PLANNER

steps.label: launch PLANNER with SotaWiki
steps.say: Flow Engine starts the Planner role on Spot and injects your SotaWiki Knowledge Engine map so any BYOK model starts knowing your module layout.
steps.screen: Spot Planner running: reading SotaWiki & repo tree (read-only)

steps.label: post flow-plan & pause
steps.say: The Planner posts a flow-plan checklist comment naming the target files and acceptance criteria, then sets flow:needs-approval for human review.
steps.screen:
Comment by bot: flow-plan Task Ledger (3 work packages)
Label updated: flow:needs-approval

sections.title: J3: Warm worktrees and QA isolation
intro: Approving a plan starts the Developer role. Developer turns can reuse a warm Spot machine inside fresh git worktrees, but Evaluator is strictly blocked from reusing a Developer machine.
sections.screenLabel: What you see on the Pull Request

steps.label: add label flow:approved
steps.say: You review the plan and add flow:approved (or comment approve). Flow Engine mints a single-run credential for the Developer turn.
steps.screen: Issue #42 approved: dispatching DEVELOPER turn

steps.label: POST /v1/runs/{id}/llm-key
steps.say: The Spot machine claims its decrypted model key once, binding the credential to its cloud instance ID so no other machine can reuse it.
steps.screen: KMS Key Claimed: bound to EC2 X-Instance-ID i-0a9f...

steps.label: push branch & post flow-ack
steps.say: The Developer writes tests first, implements the change, opens a pull request, and posts a flow-ack summary while streaming live telemetry.
steps.screen: PR #48 Opened: feat: add circuit breaker · flow-ack posted

steps.label: comment @atobar-flow-agent
steps.say: You can steer an active or paused pull request at any time in plain English by commenting to the agent on the PR thread.
steps.screen: You commented: @atobar-flow-agent use exponential jitter in store.py

steps.label: POST /turn-complete
steps.say: When the Developer finishes, Flow Engine checks WARM_HANDOVER_FORBIDDEN_ROLES. Because the next role is Evaluator, it orders the Developer machine to shut down.
steps.screen: Zero-Trust Guard: WARM_HANDOVER_FORBIDDEN_ROLES = {evaluator, arbitrator} → terminate Dev VM

sections.title: J4: Two-stage visual QA on Spot
intro: The Evaluator always boots on a clean Spot machine with a read-only GitHub token. It checks code citations first, then starts the real app inside an X11 desktop to capture verified screenshots.
sections.screenLabel: What happens inside the Evaluator VM

steps.label: cold boot on head_sha
steps.say: The fresh Evaluator machine checks out the exact pull request commit, waits for GitHub Actions CI, and verifies Stage 1 file and line citations.
steps.screen: Stage 1 Static Check: verified file:src/store.py#L42-L68 on head_sha 9c4e1a2

steps.label: boot app in X11 + xwininfo
steps.say: In Stage 2, the Evaluator starts the app inside X11. It runs xwininfo and process checks to prove a real window is open.
steps.screen: X11 Display :99: Chromium window 1440x900 verified via xwininfo & ps

steps.label: POST /screenshots (PNG + sha256)
steps.say: The Evaluator uploads encrypted PNG screenshots tagged with their SHA-256 digest, window list, and data mode to the Control Panel.
steps.screen: Uploaded PNG: sha256:e3b0c4... · data_mode: live

steps.label: post flow-verdict: approved
steps.say: Once static and visual checks pass, the Evaluator posts the flow-verdict comment with embedded screenshots and marks the check run green.
steps.screen: PR #48 Verdict: flow-verdict: approved (with live X11 screenshot proof)

sections.title: J5: Deterministic metric gate, auto-merge, and living SotaWiki
intro: No language model ever decides whether code merges. Flow Engine runs a pure Python metric gate on verified CI numbers, merges the PR, and refreshes the repository wiki.
sections.screenLabel: What happens at the merge gate

steps.label: POST /v1/metrics (flow-metrics.json)
steps.say: Your repository's flow-metrics.yml workflow runs on GitHub Actions and sends signed metric observations to the Control Panel.
steps.screen: CI Metrics Verified: test_pass_rate = 1.0 (threshold >= 1.0)

steps.label: arbitrate(policy, observations)
steps.say: Flow Engine runs the pure Python function arbitrate to compare every metric observation against the tenant policy and record turn spend in loop_rounds.
steps.screen: Pure Python Arbitrator: all required metrics & guardrails passed

steps.label: squash-merge PR & queue SotaWiki
steps.say: Under auto-merge mode, Flow Engine squash-merges the pull request and queues a coalesced SotaWiki Knowledge Engine refresh after N merges.
steps.screen: PR #48 Squash-Merged: Knowledge Engine refresh queued after N merges

sections.title: J6: Goal completion, circuit breakers, and 1-commit clean exit
intro: After every merge, Flow Engine checks repository goals and enforces hard cost and round circuit breakers. At any time, deleting two workflow files detaches the repo cleanly.
sections.screenLabel: What you see at goal completion & exit

steps.label: goal_step() & circuit breakers
steps.say: After each merge, goal_step checks default-branch metrics against tenant_goals while circuit breakers cap per-PR cost and review rounds.
steps.screen: Outer Goal Loop: all target metrics met · regression guardrails active

steps.label: git rm 2 workflow YAML files
steps.say: When you hand off or sunset a repository, you delete flow-trigger.yml and flow-metrics.yml in one commit. Zero lock-in remains.
steps.screen: 1-Commit Clean Exit: git rm .github/workflows/flow-trigger.yml flow-metrics.yml

sections.title: Nano Harness: How NanobotRuntime runs a role inside Spot
intro: Above the sandbox, Flow Engine is 100% deterministic Python. Inside the Spot sandbox, NanobotRuntime drives the nanobot-ai loop inside an isolated home folder with server-side tool guards and live cost tracking.

steps.label: start Spot role task
steps.say: Flow Engine starts a role on Spot. Spot Runner creates nanobot_home outside the client git folder and writes SOUL.md.
steps.screen:
Workspace Split (J44): /flow-run/agent_ws/SOUL.md ≠ /worktrees/client-repo
.git/info/exclude blocks .nanobot/ & SOUL.md from commits

steps.label: bind RAM keys & SotaWiki
steps.say: NanobotRuntime binds memory-only key placeholders and Phase-0 SotaWiki context so any BYOK model follows your repo's best practices.
steps.screen: RAM Keys + Knowledge Engine: ${FLOW_LLM_API_KEY} + SotaWiki injected

steps.label: call stdio MCP tool
steps.say: The model calls a tool. tools_mcp checks the role allowlist in a separate process before running the command.
steps.screen: FastMCP Allowlist: disabledSkills: ["github"] · role tools enforced

steps.label: view_image() X11 PNG
steps.say: During visual checks, view_image reads X11 screenshots inside the workspace so the model inspects real pixels.
steps.screen: Multimodal Vision: view_image(.atobar/artifacts/x11_window.png)

steps.label: stream heartbeat & $
steps.say: After every model turn, FlowHook sends a 15-second heartbeat, resets the 900-second stall timer, and updates pull request spend.
steps.screen: Pinned PR Telemetry: Turn 6 · 41.2k tokens · $0.38 · heartbeat OK

steps.label: return verified envelope
steps.say: When the role finishes, NanobotRuntime checks the fenced output block and reports completion back to Flow Engine.
steps.screen: Envelope Verified: flow-ack / flow-verdict schema passed

takeaway: ATOBAR (Agentic Teams On BYOK And Repos) keeps your repo 100% standard GitHub. Isolated Spot roles write and visually test code, pure Python gates merge it, and two YAML files detach in one commit.
